title: Refining a quotient section to an etale pair neighbourhood
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring, $J$ an ideal, and $i=(B\to C)$ an etale neighbourhood of the pair: its structure map is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $B/J\to C/JC$ is bijective. Let $g:C\to D$ be an etale ring map and $s:D\to B/J$ a ring map whose composite with $B\to C\to D$ is the quotient map. Then there is another neighbourhood $N$ of the pair, a morphism $j:i\to N$ in the full category under $B$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and maps $k:D\to N$ and $r:N\to B/J$ such that $k g=j$, $r$ fixes $B$, and $r k=s$.

proof.text: Compose the etale maps B to C and C to D. The section s to B/J fixes B by hypothesis. It kills JD: the kernel ideal contains every image of J and hence the ideal they generate. Factor through D/JD and extend scalars along B to B/J. The quotient is etale by the tensor-quotient equivalence and base change.

Apply idempotent splitting to the section on D/JD, choose an idempotent e mapping to 1 and an equivalence of its localization with B/J. Lift e to a in D. Set L=D[1/a]. Localization and composition make L etale over B. The section extends to r:L to B/J because s(a)=1.

The quotient localization instance identifies L/(JD)L as a localization of D/JD away from e. The identity (JD)L=JL and the splitting equivalence yield L/JL isomorphic to B/J as a B/J-algebra. Thus the canonical quotient map is bijective (the inverse of this algebra equivalence fixes the base). Take L as N, the localization map as k, and the composite C to L as j. Scalar-tower identities show k g=j and r fixes B; the localization lift equation shows r k=s.

lean.statement:
theorem etale_section_neighbourhood_refinement (B : Type u) [CommRing B] (J : Ideal B)
    (i : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of B) ↦
        AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map C.hom) ∧
          Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (J.map C.hom.hom) C.hom.hom
            Ideal.le_comap_map)))
    (D : Type u) [CommRing D] (g : i.obj.right →+* D)
    (hd : let : Algebra i.obj.right D := g.toAlgebra
      Algebra.Etale i.obj.right D)
    (s : D →+* B ⧸ J)
    (hs : (s.comp g).comp i.obj.hom.hom = Ideal.Quotient.mk J) :
    ∃ (N : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of B) ↦
        AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map C.hom) ∧
          Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (J.map C.hom.hom) C.hom.hom
            Ideal.le_comap_map)))
      (j : i ⟶ N) (k : D →+* N.obj.right) (r : N.obj.right →+* B ⧸ J),
      k.comp g = j.hom.right.hom ∧
        r.comp N.obj.hom.hom = Ideal.Quotient.mk J ∧ r.comp k = s
